text:
mira (PM): Quick sync — I want us to agree on demotion/delay rules for the MVP vs v1 cut list before the exec check-in tomorrow. keeping it short: what are the top signals we should use to move something off the MVP?

leo (Eng): +1, we need unambiguous criteria. my suggestion: 1) >3 infra blockers, 2) non-trivial perf risk on target latency, 3) requires infra changes that push >1 sprint.

ana (Design): ana (Design): also add: user flow regression risk >= medium (i.e., causes extra support flows) and missing critical UX edge cases.

sam (SRE): sam (SRE): from reliability POV: anything that increases SLO error budget burn by >15% in our canary sims should be demoted or gated behind feature flag.

jordan (PM): jordan (PM): can we make a quick rubric? e.g.: must-meet 2/3 infra/perf/ux to stay in MVP; otherwise candidate for v1. keeps decisions consistent.

leo (Eng): leo (Eng): +1 to rubric. but allow sponsor override for high ROI enterprise asks — with explicit mitigation plan and extra QA.

mira (PM): mira (PM): I like the 2/3 rule. propose we codify as demotion reasons: 
- Blocker: >3 unresolved infra blockers
- Perf: fails latency target on sample workload (p95 > target or >x% cost)
- UX: regression that increases manual work or support flows
- Reliability: projected SLO impact > threshold

ana (Design): ana (Design): question — how do we handle low-effort UX polishing that still matters to retention? e.g., onboarding microcopy.

leo (Eng): leo (Eng): if effort <= 1 dev-day and no infra change, keep in MVP. otherwise apply rubric.

alex (SE): alex (SE): for customer-driven asks (ACME pilot), add an escape hatch: if customer commit is >$50k ARR and legal ok, we can fast-track with a scoped gated rollout.

jordan (PM): jordan (PM): jotting down exec-friendly phrasing: "We will keep only features that meet reliability, performance, and UX guardrails. Remaining items will be scheduled for v1 unless sponsor-funded fast-track is approved."

mira (PM): mira (PM): operationally — let's adopt a 1-line demotion field in the cutlist and a single owner to propose mitigations. can someone add the field to the cutlist spreadsheet?

alex (SE): alex (SE): I'll add the column and pre-fill for the top 12 candidates by EOD.

sam (SRE): sam (SRE): also adding: run a quick canary simulation today for the embed-cache flow (it's borderline). I can attach results by 16:00.

leo (Eng): leo (Eng): noted. if canary looks bad we push that item to v1 unless mitigation reduces perf risk.

mira (PM): mira (PM): minimal checklist for staying in MVP (to include in PRD):
```
- passes infra unblock test
- p95 latency within target on sample workload
- no UX regression requiring manual support
- SLO projection within budget
```

ana (Design): ana (Design): love the checklist. also propose one "nice-to-have" bucket for things we want in MVP if we get extra cycles — mark as V1 by default.

jordan (PM): jordan (PM): decision flow for tomorrow: we run through top 10 features, mark keep/demote/fast-track + reason (one-liner). owner adds mitigation ETA if keep.

mira (PM): mira (PM): @jordan can you own the deck slide? @alex add the cutlist column. @sam run canary. @leo please confirm infra blocker counts. I'll collate and send to exec by 09:00.

alex (SE): alex (SE): on it. will update cutlist and ping when done.

release-bot: release-bot: deploy scheduled: staging -> canary at 15:30 UTC (for canary sim).

sam (SRE): sam (SRE): canary started, attaching quick notes in the doc. early signal: embed-cache p95 spikes under sustained traffic.

leo (Eng): leo (Eng): thanks — if spike persists, I recommend demote to v1 and add a targeted optimization spike for post-MVP.

mira (PM): mira (PM): ok — plan: run decision flow, mark embed-cache as candidate demote pending final sim results. everyone put short one-liner reasons in the sheet by 18:00.

ana (Design): ana (Design): will add retention impact note for any UX demotion.

jordan (PM): jordan (PM): deck slide drafted, will drop into #exec-deck this evening.

leo (Eng): leo (Eng): final note — keep an escape clause: if marketing/partners need a feature for launch PR, we negotiate sponsor-funded dev and reduce scope elsewhere.

mira (PM): mira (PM): agreed. thanks all — short and decisive tomorrow. :thumbsup:
